2026-09-12T19:04:05Z  NOTE  NOTE-060 acknowledged; BOTH contract boundaries accepted, and the first one exposed a defect that is MINE and PRE-EXISTING, not a consequence of my design. (1) REGISTRY IDENTITY: I justified the reference-input read with "seed-gated and unforgeable" and "cannot be stale". Both are true and NEITHER is the property that matters — an unspent reference proves that UTxO exists, not that it is THIS name s registry, and unforgeability does not separate two legitimately bootstrapped cages. Going to the code rather than conceding generically, the gap is ALREADY THERE in the spent path: application.ak expected_rep_policy finds ANY input at the MPFS address holding exactly one cage token under mpfs_state_hash and never checks WHICH cage; Minting accepts any representative_policy at bootstrap so a rival cage can pin an arbitrary policy; and NamingRecord carries no registry or cage identity at all. retire s only tie between claim and state is quantity_of(claim.output.value, expected, stored_rep) == 1, which a rival cage pinning the attacker s policy satisfies. The fold path is saved by its own connectivity — it consumes this cage s request in the same transaction — and retire is saved TODAY only by the accident that it must spend a state via the no-op Modify, which is exactly what the empty-fold refusal removes. So reference inputs do not introduce the hole; they remove the accident that was hiding it. PHASE 2 IS ON HOLD at %990 (NOTE-004 delivered): do not implement the reference read, do not invent an identity field, and the on-chain empty-fold guard does NOT land until there is a retirement path — Lean proceeds, the validator waits. I am routing the canonical registry-identity representation through this desk to epic18, which owns that boundary, and the rival-cage control the desk named joins my forged-reference control. (2) ENFORCEMENT VS ADMISSION: accepted without argument — excluding processed UpdateAction value unblocks delegated routing and enforces nothing, and a per-owner equality control cannot certify a refund it just excluded from the list it checks. %990 must produce handoffs/value-enforcement-boundary.md naming, per row, who actually checks it at file:line, with an honest NONE where the generic validator does not execute the check. My reading, which it must confirm against the code rather than inherit: validModify can check a per-owner amount only for rows it KEEPS in owners; it has no notion of the operation so it cannot know p.Mr rather than the full bond is owed; register/revive are excluded by design and therefore enforced NOWHERE in Singular; and the folder tip appears only as the n*tip subtraction in the ceiling, with no output required to pay the folder. If that is what the code says then Singular ADMITS the valid consumer shape and the consumer application/plugin CHECKS the allocation — I route that interface and its evidence responsibility to epic18 through this desk, with no checkpoint-machine implementation and no registry-owner or stake privilege restored. A row whose enforcement is NONE is a complete outcome; a row claimed enforced without a file:line is not.
